chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who passes by the water well and there is no bucket with him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not upon him that he descends into the water well. Indeed, the Lord of the water is the Lord of the earth, so let him perform Tayammum.'
ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to perform Tayammum instead of using water for ritual purity?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the obligation of using water is contingent upon ease of access; thus, if retrieving water requires disproportionate effort or equipment not readily available, one may resort to Tayammum. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'ease in difficulty' (al-taklif bi-ma la yutaq), ensuring that ritual purity remains accessible without undue hardship. The phrase 'Lord of the water is the Lord of the earth' highlights the divine source of both elements, validating the earth as a valid substitute for water when the latter is inaccessible.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Husayn Bin Abu Al A’ala who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the man who passes by the water well and there is no bucket with him (to draw the water with)’. Heasws said: ‘It is not upon him that he descends into the water well. The Lordazwj of the water, Heazwj is (also) the Lordazwj of the earth. So let him perform Tayammum’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Husayn ibn abu af-‘Afa’ who has said the foflowing:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who passes by a well but does not have a bucket (to draw water). He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not necessary for him to climb down the well; the Lord of water is the Lord the earth; he must take Tayammum.’”
